generated_plan.learning_plan_title: 3-Month Accelerated Plan for Data Analyst / Analytics Engineer / AI Engineer (Global Market)
general_advice: Prioritize Learning by Doing: Spend more time coding, building, and debugging than just consuming content.
Document Everything: Create clear READMEs for your GitHub projects, explaining your thought process, challenges, and solutions.
Network Actively: Connect with professionals on LinkedIn, follow industry leaders, and engage in online communities.
Stay Updated: The data/AI field is dynamic. Read blogs, follow news, and explore new tools.
Focus on Problem Solving: Understand the 'why' behind techniques, not just the 'how'.
Balance & Well-being: Avoid burnout. Take regular breaks and maintain a healthy routine.
Be Flexible: This plan is a guideline. Adjust it based on your learning pace, interests, and career aspirations. It is recommended to choose 1-2 primary paths for deeper specialization after Month 1.

daily_study_breakdown.hands_on_practice: 1.5 - 2 hours (Coding exercises, SQL queries, tool practice)
daily_study_breakdown.project_work_review_problem_solving: 1 hour (Building, debugging, documenting, reviewing, or networking)

monthly_breakdown.focus: Foundational Skills & Data Fundamentals (Common to all roles)

sub_topics: Basic to Intermediate SQL (SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, JOINs (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL), UNION, Subqueries, Common aggregate functions)
practice: LeetCode SQL (Easy/Medium)
StrataScratch (basic)
HackerRank SQL
Work with diverse public datasets

sub_topics: Pandas DataFrames/Series
Data loading (CSV, Excel)
Indexing, selection, filtering, grouping, merging, pivoting
Cleaning missing data, basic feature engineering
NumPy arrays for numerical operations
practice: Kaggle notebooks (explore and replicate analyses)
Small data cleaning projects
resources: "Python for Data Analysis" by Wes McKinney

sub_topics: Creating various plot types (scatter, line, bar, histogram, box plot)
Customizing plots, understanding visualization best practices
Telling a story with data
practice: Visualize a dataset from Kaggle
Practice explaining insights from visualizations
resources: "Storytelling with Data" by Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic (book for concepts)

sub_topics: Descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, variance, std dev)
Inferential statistics (hypothesis testing basics, t-tests, ANOVA)
Probability distributions (normal, binomial)
Git basics (init, add, commit, push, pull, branch, merge)
practice: Apply statistical tests to small datasets
Set up a Git repository for all your projects, practice branching and merging
weeks.mini_project: End of Month 1: Create a small data analysis project. Clean a dataset, perform EDA, visualize findings, and upload it to GitHub with a clear README.

monthly_breakdown.decision_point: By the end of Month 1, you should have a clearer idea of which role(s) (Data Analyst, Analytics Engineer, or AI Engineer) you find most appealing. It's recommended to pick 1-2 primary paths for deeper specialization in Month 2.

sub_topics: Window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, LAG, LEAD)
Common Table Expressions (CTEs)
Stored Procedures/Functions (basics)
Performance Tuning SQL queries
Introduction to Data Warehousing (DW) concepts (STAR/Snowflake schema, Kimball methodology, OLAP vs OLTP)
practice: Complex SQL challenges (e.g., Maven Analytics, advanced LeetCode SQL)
Design a simple star schema for a business scenario
resources: Blog posts on DW design principles

weeks.topic: Business Intelligence Tools (Tableau/Power BI) / ETL with dbt (for AE)
sub_topics: For Data Analyst: Hands-on with Tableau or Power BI (creating dashboards, interactive visualizations, calculated fields).
For Analytics Engineer: Introduction to dbt (data build tool) for data transformation, modularity, testing, and documentation in SQL.
practice: DA: Build a complex interactive dashboard on a public dataset.
AE: Implement a small data pipeline using dbt to transform raw data.

weeks.topic: Cloud Data Warehouses & Data Modeling (for AE) / A/B Testing & Communication (for DA)
sub_topics: For Analytics Engineer: Overview of cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift), practical exposure to one (e.g., BigQuery free tier). Data Modeling best practices.
For Data Analyst: Fundamentals of A/B testing, hypothesis formulation, interpreting results. Focusing on clear, concise communication of insights to non-technical stakeholders.
practice: AE: Load data into a cloud DW, run complex queries.
DA: Analyze an A/B test dataset, prepare a presentation with recommendations.

sub_topics: Start a significant end-to-end project showcasing your chosen specialization.
project_ideas: **DA Project:** Find a messy business dataset (e.g., customer churn, sales data), clean it, perform in-depth exploratory data analysis, build a compelling interactive dashboard (Tableau/Power BI), and present findings with actionable recommendations.

**AE Project:** Design and implement a small data pipeline that extracts data from a source (e.g., CSV, public API), loads it into a cloud data warehouse, transforms it using dbt, and makes it ready for analytics. Document the pipeline thoroughly.

weeks.topic: Advanced Machine Learning & Deep Learning Refresher
sub_topics: Review of ML concepts (supervised, unsupervised), deeper dive into DL architectures (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers basics).
Reinforcement Learning basics.
Revisit TensorFlow, introduce PyTorch (if new) – understanding their ecosystems.
practice: Implement more complex models (e.g., image classification with a pre-trained CNN, simple sequence prediction with RNN).
Experiment with transfer learning.
resources: "Deep Learning with Python" by Francois Chollet

sub_topics: Introduction to MLOps concepts (model versioning, reproducibility, deployment).
Docker for containerization.
Building simple APIs for model inference using Flask/FastAPI.
practice: Containerize a trained model using Docker.
Build a simple web API to serve predictions from your model locally.

weeks.topic: MLOps - Monitoring, CI/CD for ML & Cloud ML Platforms
sub_topics: Model monitoring (data/concept drift detection basics), CI/CD principles for ML (testing code, data, models).
Overview of cloud ML platforms (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, Azure ML) - focus on one free tier for hands-on.
practice: Set up a basic CI/CD pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions) for your model code.
Deploy a simple model using a cloud ML platform's free tier (e.g., GCP Vertex AI Workbench).
resources: Cloud provider ML documentation (e.g., GCP MLOps guides)

sub_topics: Start a significant end-to-end project showcasing your chosen specialization.
project_ideas: **AI Engineer Project:** Choose a dataset (e.g., image classification, NLP sentiment analysis). Build, train, and evaluate a robust deep learning model. Containerize it with Docker, build a FastAPI/Flask endpoint, and deploy it (e.g., on a cloud free tier or services like Render for simplicity). Implement basic model versioning or monitoring.

monthly_breakdown.focus: Portfolio Building, Advanced Topics & Interview Preparation

weeks.topic: Advanced Topics / Deep Dive into Chosen Role
sub_topics: **DA/AE:** Advanced analytical techniques, stakeholder management, dashboard optimization, advanced data governance concepts, data observability.

**AI Eng:** More advanced ML algorithms (e.g., transformers for NLP, advanced CV architectures), distributed ML (basics of Spark/Dask for large datasets), ethical AI considerations, advanced system design for ML.
**ALL:** Work on a second, more complex project in your chosen area, or significantly refine your first project. Aim to solve a real-world problem or replicate a research paper.
practice: Deep dive into a specific sub-area of interest (e.g., time series analysis for DA/AE, generative AI for AI Eng).
Enhance current projects with more features, better performance, or more robust testing.

sub_topics: Polish your GitHub portfolio (ensure clear READMEs, well-commented code, relevant links).
Create a professional LinkedIn profile (highlight skills, projects, network).
Build a simple personal website/blog to showcase projects (optional but recommended for global market), hosting your resume and project links.
action: Review and refine all project documentation and code.
Start connecting with professionals and recruiters on LinkedIn.

sub_topics: **DA/AE:** Advanced SQL (LeetCode/StrataScratch), Python for Data (Pandas exercises, data manipulation), case study questions (how would you approach a business problem?), dashboard design discussions.

**AI Eng:** Algorithms & Data Structures (LeetCode Medium), Python coding, ML fundamentals (theory, model selection, metrics), ML System Design (how to build an ML system for X problem, scaling, monitoring).
**ALL:** Practice explaining your projects concisely, highlighting your contributions, technical challenges, and business impact.
practice: Consistent practice of coding problems (LeetCode, HackerRank).
Reviewing fundamental concepts and common interview questions for your chosen role.

sub_topics: Common behavioral questions (STAR method).
Resume & cover letter optimization (tailor to each application).
For AI Eng: Deeper dive into system design principles relevant to ML (scalability, reliability, latency, cost).
Networking and job application strategies.
action: Conduct mock interviews (with peers, mentors, or online platforms).
Start actively applying to relevant roles.
Attend virtual meetups, webinars, or career fairs related to your chosen field.
Refine your elevator pitch for your skills and aspirations.
